definitions.explanation: The way something is done or appears.
Used as a suffix to indicate the first time in a while.

examples.japanese: {身振|みぶ}り{手振|てぶ}りで{伝|つた}えた。
examples.notes: {身振|みぶ}り{手振|てぶ}り = gestures, body language

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いは{立派|りっぱ}だった。
{大人|おとな}らしい{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}いを{心|こころ}がけている。
examples.english: I try to act in an adult-like manner.

examples.notes: 〜{振|ふ}りをする = to pretend to ~

examples.japanese: {見|み}て{見|み}ぬ{振|ふ}りをするのはよくない。
examples.english: It's not good to pretend not to see things.
examples.notes: {見|み}て{見|み}ぬ{振|ふ}り = pretending not to see, turning a blind eye

examples.japanese: {寝|ね}た{振|ふ}りをして{様子|ようす}を{窺|うかが}った。
examples.english: I pretended to be asleep and observed the situation.
We met for the first time in three years.
examples.notes: As time suffix, read ぶり

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}し{振|ぶ}りに{映画|えいが}を{見|み}に{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went to see a movie for the first time in a while.

examples.japanese: 10{年|ねん}{振|ぶ}りに{故郷|こきょう}に{帰|かえ}ったら、{町|まち}がすっかり{変|か}わっていた。
examples.english: When I returned to my hometown for the first time in ten years, the town had completely changed.

notes:
Has multiple related meanings centered on appearance/manner.

MEANING 1 - MANNER:
・{身振|みぶ}り{手振|てぶ}り (gestures)
・{振|ふ}る{舞|ま}い (behavior, conduct)

MEANING 2 - PRETENSE:
・〜{振|ふ}りをする (to pretend to ~)
・{知|し}らん{振|ぷ}り (pretending not to know)
・{見|み}て{見|み}ぬ{振|ふ}り (pretending not to see)

MEANING 3 - TIME SUFFIX:
・〜{振|ぶ}り (for the first time in ~)
・3{年|ねん}{振|ぶ}り (for the first time in 3 years)
・{久|ひさ}し{振|ぶ}り (after a long time)

NOTE:
As a time suffix, it's often read ぶり rather than ふり.
